summary: The results demonstrate that GRASP learns to encode bond connectivity topology in its CLS tokens, distinguishing topological isomers (same atoms/types, different bonds) where simple composition-based features fail.

claims.claim: Pretrained GRASP encodes heavy-atom connectivity topology distinct from atomic composition.
claims.evidence: pretrained_cls_12 AUROC 0.769 ± 0.023 vs bag_of_tokens AUROC 0.500 ± 0.000; pretrained_cls_12 cosine distance 0.183 vs bag_of_tokens 0.0.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C,N,O,S]` (atom types only). Prediction: If model relies on composition, AUROC ≈ 0.5.
claims.prediction: If the model relied solely on Crippen atom counts or Lipinski MW, `bag_of_tokens` would achieve high AUROC (>0.7) because token match fraction is 1.0 for all pairs. The observed 0.5 confirms reliance on graph structure.

claims.claim: Topology encoding requires pretraining; random initialization yields weak signal.
claims.evidence: random_cls_12 AUROC 0.567 ± 0.036 vs pretrained_cls_12 AUROC 0.769 ± 0.023; distance 0.002 (random) vs 0.183 (pretrained).
claims.test: Label: `model_type` column ('random' vs 'pretrained'). Prediction: Random AUROC < 0.65.
claims.prediction: If topology were inherent in positional encodings or random weights, distance would be >0.1 and AUROC >0.7 regardless of pretraining.

claims.claim: Layer-12 CLS tokens capture connectivity changes more strongly than Layer-6 mean pooling for the best checkpoint (`a1`).
claims.test: Layer index column (6 or 12). Prediction: Layer-12 CLS separation > Layer-6 Mean for `a1`.
claims.prediction: If early layers integrated global topology better than final aggregation, mean[6] would outperform cls[12]. Here a1_cls_12 dominates.

claims.claim: The rewiring operation alters local steric and electronic environments without changing functional group identity.
claims.evidence: Token match fraction 1.0; `bag_of_tokens` AUROC 0.5 implies no atom type changes (HBA/HBD/MW constant).
claims.test: RDKit: `Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)` -> `GetNumHeavyAtoms()` and `CalcCrippenDescriptors()`. Prediction: Descriptors identical for original/rewired pairs.
claims.prediction: If descriptors changed, bag-of-tokens might succeed. Since it fails at 0.5, the model detects changes in bond paths (e.g., linear vs branched alkyl chains) rather than functional groups.

trivial_explanations: The `bag_of_tokens` result of AUROC 0.5 confirms that atom counts and types are identical for original/rewired pairs; thus, the model's success is not due to trivial features like MW or HBA/HBD.
Random-init models show slight signal (AUROC ~0.57) suggesting positional encodings provide weak topological cues even without learning weights.
